metadata.title: Label the Five Supervisory Capacities in a Build Session with Claude Code

beats.narration_text: A forty-minute build session contains exactly five supervisory moves. Each one named, each one preventing a specific failure that shipped to the student without it. This is Liam, in for Bear.

The five capacities: Problem Formulation, Plausibility Auditing, Tool Orchestration, Interpretive Judgment, Executive Integration. They have always existed in competent software work — Claude makes their absence costly.

items.label: PF — Problem Formulation
items.sub: Decide what the build is before Claude sees it.

items.label: PA — Plausibility Auditing
items.sub: Hear the wrong note before the tests confirm it.

items.label: TO — Tool Orchestration
items.sub: Which task, in what order, trusted how far.

items.label: IJ — Interpretive Judgment
items.sub: Supply the meaning the number cannot carry.

items.label: EI — Executive Integration
items.sub: Hold the whole build toward one goal.

beats.narration_text: We run a GPA sorting session with each supervisory move explicitly labeled before it happens.

props.command:
claude "[PF] Write top_three_by_gpa with tie-breaking by last_name.
  Test set MUST include: at least one tie case (same GPA).
[PA] After output: run tie-case probe immediately.
[TO] If probe fails: re-prompt with exact failure description.
[IJ] Interpret any accuracy threshold before accepting.
[EI] Final: confirm all user needs from SDD are met."

beats.narration_text: PF: test set must include a tie case before output is accepted. PA: probe with tie case immediately after generation. TO: re-prompt with specific failure description. IJ: interpret the 85% accuracy threshold in context.

props.code:
# Labeled Build Transcript — GPA Sort Session

[PF] Before prompt: required tie case in test set
  - test_tie: Bell 3.92, Adams 3.92 -> Adams first

[PA] After output: probe with tie case IMMEDIATELY
  - Result: Bell returned first (bug found)

[TO] Re-prompt with exact failure:
  'Bell and Adams tie at 3.92, Adams should rank
   first (alphabetical), got Bell — fix sort key'

[IJ] 85% accuracy threshold in context:
  - 15% failure rate on tie cases = unacceptable
  - threshold requires domain interpretation

[EI] Final: all SDD needs confirmed satisfied

beats.narration_text: The labeled transcript reads back cleanly. PF at the start — tie case required. PA immediately after — tie probe run. The probe finds the bug. TO — re-prompt names the exact failure: Bell and Adams tie at three point nine two, Adams should rank first, got Bell. IJ — the eighty-five percent accuracy figure requires domain interpretation before accepting.

props.caption: Labeled run: bug caught before ship.
props.code:
[PF] tie case required .......... OK
[PA] tie probe: Bell 3.92, Adams 3.92
     expected: Adams  got: Bell   ← BUG
[TO] re-prompt sent (exact failure named)
     patched sort key: (-gpa, last_name)
[PA] re-probe: Adams first, Bell second
     expected: Adams  got: Adams  ← PASS
[IJ] 85% accuracy: 15% miss on ties = fail
     threshold requires domain read
[EI] SDD needs: all confirmed satisfied

result: NOT SHIPPED (fixed)

beats.narration_text: We run the same build without supervisory labeling and identify the step where the unlabeled session would have shipped the bug.

props.command: claude "Run the same GPA sort build WITHOUT supervisory labels.\nAt which step would the tie-breaking bug have shipped?\nShow the unlabeled decision point where the failure entered."

beats.narration_text: Unlabeled session: no tie case in the initial test set. Output accepted. Build ships. The bug appears in production when a real tie occurs. The only difference between the sessions is the PF move at the start — requiring a tie case before accepting output.

props.caption: Unlabeled run: bug ships.
props.code:
test set: 12 pairs, no tie cases
tests: 12 / 12 pass
output: accepted
commit: main

delta from labeled run: the PF move.
